name: Palm Oil
description: High in saturated fatty acids (~50%). Linked to elevated LDL cholesterol if consumed in high quantities.

name: Soy Lecithin
description: Common food emulsifier derived from soybeans. Contains trace soy proteins.

name: Maltodextrin
description: High glycemic index carbohydrate (GI 85-105). Can cause rapid blood glucose spikes.

name: Monosodium Glutamate
description: Umami flavor enhancer. Recognized as safe by major food safety authorities.

name: High Fructose Corn Syrup
description: Caloric sweetener linked to increased risk of metabolic syndrome and hepatic steatosis when overconsumed.

name: Sugar
description: Provides empty calories with no nutritional value. Excess consumption linked to obesity, type-2 diabetes, and dental caries.

name: Salt
description: Essential mineral but excess sodium (>2.3 g/day) is associated with hypertension and cardiovascular disease.

name: Whole Wheat Flour
description: Rich in dietary fiber, vitamins, and minerals. Contains gluten — not suitable for celiac patients.

name: Wheat Flour
description: Refined wheat flour stripped of bran and germ. Contains gluten. Lower fiber than whole wheat.

name: Skimmed Milk Powder
description: Contains lactose and milk proteins (casein, whey). Major allergen for lactose-intolerant individuals.

name: Hazelnuts
description: Major tree nut allergen. Rich in healthy monounsaturated fats, vitamin E, and antioxidants.

name: Sodium Benzoate
description: Antimicrobial preservative. Combined with vitamin C (ascorbic acid), it can form benzene — a known carcinogen.

name: Potassium Sorbate
description: Widely used mold and yeast inhibitor in baked goods, dairy, and beverages. Considered safe at approved levels.

name: Sodium Nitrate
description: Used in cured meats to prevent bacterial growth. Can form nitrosamines (potential carcinogens) under high heat.

name: BHA
description: Synthetic antioxidant to prevent rancidity. Listed as possibly carcinogenic to humans (IARC Group 2B).

name: BHT
description: Synthetic antioxidant used in fats and oils. Some animal studies suggest endocrine disruption at high doses.

name: Aspartame
description: 200x sweeter than sugar. Contains phenylalanine — contraindicated for PKU patients. IARC classified possibly carcinogenic (2B, 2023).

name: Saccharin
description: Oldest artificial sweetener. 300-500x sweeter than sugar. Bitter aftertaste at high concentrations.

name: Sucralose
description: 600x sweeter than sugar. Passes through the body largely unmetabolized. Considered safe by major health agencies.

name: Stevia
description: Plant-derived natural zero-calorie sweetener from Stevia rebaudiana. 200-300x sweeter than sugar.

name: Xylitol
description: Natural sugar alcohol with 40% fewer calories than sugar. Dental-friendly. Toxic to dogs — keep away from pets.

name: Sorbitol
description: 60% as sweet as sugar with fewer calories. Can cause digestive discomfort in large quantities (>50g/day).

name: Carrageenan
description: Seaweed-derived thickener used in dairy alternatives and processed meats. Some studies link degraded form to inflammation.

name: Mono and Diglycerides
description: Common emulsifiers derived from fats. May contain small amounts of trans fats not required to be labeled.

name: Tartrazine
description: Yellow synthetic azo dye. Linked to hyperactivity in children. Requires warning label in EU (Southampton study).

name: Sunset Yellow
description: Orange-yellow synthetic azo dye. Part of the Southampton Six — linked to hyperactivity in children.

name: Caramel Color
description: Widely used brown colorant in cola drinks, soy sauce, and baked goods. Class IV (e150d) contains 4-MEI, a possible carcinogen.

name: Citric Acid
description: Naturally occurring acid found in citrus fruits. Widely used as an acidity regulator and natural preservative.

name: Ascorbic Acid
description: Vitamin C. Acts as an antioxidant and dough conditioner in baked goods. Essential nutrient for humans.

name: Vanillin
description: Synthetic version of the primary compound in natural vanilla extract. Used as a cost-effective vanilla substitute.

name: Natural Vanilla Extract
description: Extract from Vanilla planifolia bean pods. Contains vanillin plus hundreds of flavor compounds.

name: Cocoa Powder
description: Rich source of flavonoids and antioxidants. Processed with alkali (Dutched) cocoa has lower antioxidant content.

name: Sunflower Oil
description: High in polyunsaturated fatty acids (linoleic acid). Good source of vitamin E. Stable for high-temperature cooking.

name: Canola Oil
description: Low in saturated fat. Good source of omega-3 fatty acids (ALA). Heart-healthy cooking oil.

name: Peanuts
description: One of the top 9 major food allergens. Can cause severe anaphylaxis. Rich in protein, niacin, and monounsaturated fats.

name: Eggs
description: Major food allergen. Rich in high-quality protein, choline, and fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K).

name: Milk
description: Major food allergen containing casein and whey proteins. Also contains lactose — problematic for lactose-intolerant individuals.

name: Wheat Starch
description: Starch extracted from wheat. Contains gluten — avoid if celiac. Used as a thickener in sauces and baked goods.

name: Corn Starch
description: Gluten-free thickener and texture agent extracted from corn. Used in sauces, puddings, and coatings.

name: Sodium Bicarbonate
description: Common chemical leavening agent used in baked goods. Reacts with acids to produce CO2 for rise.

name: Whey Powder
description: By-product of cheese manufacturing. Contains lactose and milk proteins — major dairy allergen.

name: Oats
description: Naturally gluten-free but frequently cross-contaminated with wheat in processing. Rich in beta-glucan fiber.

name: Rice Flour
description: Gluten-free flour alternative commonly used in gluten-free baking products.

name: Potassium Carbonate
description: Alkaline salt used as a raising agent in baked goods and as an acidity regulator.

name: Ammonium Carbonate
description: Traditional leavening agent used in cookies and crackers. Fully decomposes during baking, leaving no residue.
